name: Certified in Cybersecurity

fee.note: U.S. list price for the Americas, Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa; EMEA pays EUR 191.04 and the UK GBP 161.19. Taxes depend on the exam location.

exam.format: Computerized adaptive test (CAT) at Pearson VUE test centers: 100–125 multiple choice and advanced items in 2 hours. Offered in English, Chinese, Japanese, German and Spanish (Chinese only in set windows).

scope: Foundational security principles, security governance and risk, identity and access management, networking and cloud security concepts, and security operations and incident response, with foundational AI topics across the outline.
requirements: No work experience or degree required; ISC2 recommends basic IT knowledge. After passing, candidates complete an application and pay the U.S. $50 annual maintenance fee; no endorsement is needed.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: The exam moved to a new outline on September 1, 2026, the first major update since the 2022 launch: business continuity, disaster recovery and incident response concepts gave way to a Security Governance domain, incident response moved into Security Operations, and cloud, zero trust and AI topics were added. Prep material written for the earlier outline does not match.

ISC2's One Million Certified in Cybersecurity program (free course and exam) closed new enrollments on May 20, 2026; exam codes it already issued must be used by December 31, 2026. New candidates pay the regular fee.

Prices and taxes follow the exam location: ISC2 lists U.S. dollars for most regions, euros for EMEA and pounds for the UK. Pearson VUE charges U.S. $50 to reschedule and U.S. $100 to cancel. Confirm at checkout.
An exam-only purchase is one attempt that must be taken within 365 days. ISC2 also sells Peace of Mind Protection (two attempts within 180 days); its price is not on the pricing page.
Staying certified: U.S. $50 a year (members who hold only CC) and 45 CPE credits per three-year cycle.
